s02.client_chat.cc_001: don't reply to this address. it won't exist tomorrow.
s02.client_chat.cc_002: you can call me cypher. on 7 march a digital artist called maya sorensen went into her studio in wedding and never came out. the room was wrecked. there was blood.
s02.client_chat.cc_003: her manager is leo brandt. he was also her ex. he controlled her contracts, her accounts, her calendar, and for two years he controlled her.
s02.client_chat.cc_004: the file has been open four weeks and nobody has taken his phone. his lawyer plays golf with people who decide things. that is the entire investigation.
s02.client_chat.cc_005: i have her phone mirrored. live, as it sits, everything on it. i can't be the one who reads it out — anonymous means worthless, and i am extremely anonymous.
s02.client_chat.cc_006: you're not anonymous. you're licensed. if you find it, it counts.
s02.client_chat.cc_007: so. do you want to see what he did to her?
s02.client_chat.cc_008: you're on it now. live feed, not a dump. what's on it is what's on it right now.
s02.client_chat.cc_009: start with friday the 7th. the last six hours are all there.
s02.interstitial.is1_002: keep going — the money is where it gets ugly. he wasn't just controlling her, he was eating her.
s02.interstitial.is1_003: her accountant worked out the shape of it in february. she didn't get to do anything about it.
s02.interstitial.is2_002: you have the theft, the threats and him inside the building at 23:40. that is more than the police assembled in four weeks.
s02.interstitial.is2_003: package it and send it. i'll give you three addresses that can't bury it.
s02.interstitial.is2_004: you can stop now. genuinely. there's nothing left in there.
s02.interstitial.is3_002: i asked you to find who killed her. not to audit a session log.
s02.closing_chat.cl_002: I'm not going to insult you by keeping the lowercase up. Hello. It's Maya.
s02.closing_chat.cl_003: He took a hundred and eighty thousand euros from me over two years, through a company he named after a bird. He kept the passwords to my own accounts on his phone. When I said I was leaving he explained, calmly, all the ways he could ruin me, and the frightening part was that he was right about every one of them.
s02.closing_chat.cl_004: So I stopped trying to leave and I disappeared instead. I wrecked my own studio. I put my own blood on my own floor. And yes — I forged the door log, because a dead woman gets believed and a living one gets a mediation appointment.
s02.closing_chat.cl_005: Everything I gave you about the money is true. Check it again if you like. He is exactly the thief you found. The only thing I invented was my body.
s02.closing_chat.cl_006: I needed someone with a licence to find it, because if the tip comes from a ghost account it goes in a drawer. I never wanted you to look past question ten. That was my mistake — I ran two days early, and I forgot I'd already had his keycard cancelled.
s02.closing_chat.cl_007: Juno thinks I'm dead. That is the price and I pay it every day. Don't tell me what it costs. I know what it costs.
s02.closing_chat.cl_008: You have all of it now. What do you do with it?
s02.closing_chat.cl_008.opt2: Only the theft. The rest stays with me.
s02.closing_chat.cl_008.opt3: Nothing. I never opened the phone.
s02.closing_chat.cl_010: Understood. I won't argue — you'd be right to.
s02.closing_chat.cl_011: He walks on the murder, of course. But the transfers stand up on their own, so he goes down anyway, just for the crime he actually committed. And I get hunted for the rest of my life by people who think I'm the monster in this. Fine. It's a cleaner ending than the one I wrote.
s02.closing_chat.cl_012: That's the coward's line and it's also the only decent one. I noticed that too.
s02.closing_chat.cl_013: He'll do four years for the money and walk out still able to say he never touched me. The murder file stays open forever with my name at the top of it. I stay dead and I stay guilty. You've given us both exactly half of what we deserve.
s02.closing_chat.cl_015: He'll go away for killing a woman who is currently reading your messages. You know that now and you're choosing it anyway, which makes it yours as much as mine. I won't pretend that's a gift. But I'll take it.
s02.closing_chat.cl_016: This account dies in about ninety seconds. You were better than I needed you to be, and that turned out to be the most expensive thing about this whole plan. Goodbye, detective.
s02.messages.sms_020: Maya — I've finished going through the Halcyon invoices. Can we speak on the phone rather than email?
s02.messages.sms_022: Not bad. Wrong. There are management fees being charged against work that was never sold.
s02.messages.sms_024: I'd rather show you than write it down. Are you free Wednesday?
s02.messages.sms_030: I am not putting the figure in a text after what I just said to you. It is all in the reconciliation and I have put it in your drive. The file is locked and the password is in your own keychain, under the drive entry. Your keychain master is the phrase you told me on the phone.
s02.messages.sms_031: I remember it. 26.02.2025. You used that date for everything and you told me like it was nothing.
s02.messages.sms_032: You did. Please don't confront him alone.
s02.messages.sms_033: Hanna — if anything happens to my accounts, everything you found is in the drive and in my keychain. You have the login.
s02.messages.sms_034: That is an alarming message to receive on a Tuesday. Call me.
s02.messages.sms_040: Maya, the install crew need the final dimensions by Friday. Rohde Berlin.
s02.messages.sms_042: Wonderful. And Maya — Leo rang me about the commission split again. I told him it is between the gallery and the artist.
s02.messages.sms_044: Maya, please call the gallery when you can. Nobody has heard from you since Friday.
s02.messages.sms_050: I've cleared my things out of the studio. I left the good clamps, you'll need them.
s02.messages.sms_051: Ines, I'm sorry. It wasn't my decision and that's not an excuse, it's just true.
s02.messages.sms_052: I know whose decision it was. That's what makes it worse. You let him make it.
s02.messages.sms_053: Someone said the police were at Uferhallen. Maya, tell me you're ok.
s02.chats.wa_001: You went to Rohde without me again.
s02.chats.wa_002: It's my show. Kasimir asked me directly.
s02.chats.wa_003: Everything about your career comes through me. That's not a preference, it's the contract you signed.
s02.chats.wa_004: I've moved the Halcyon invoicing to quarterly. Simpler for you.
s02.chats.wa_005: Simpler for who? I want to see the statements.
s02.chats.wa_006: You want to see spreadsheets? You'd have a breakdown by page two. Let me do my job.
s02.chats.wa_007: Ines is out. She's been talking about our arrangements to people outside the studio.
s02.chats.wa_008: She's the only person who can build the piece. And she hasn't said anything to anyone.
s02.chats.wa_009: She goes. This isn't a discussion, Maya, it's a decision that's already happened.
s02.chats.wa_010: Why is Hanna Vogt asking my office for invoice records.
s02.chats.wa_011: Because she's my accountant and they're my invoices.
s02.chats.wa_012: Last time. Pull her off it.
s02.chats.wa_014: Then understand what you're choosing. I can end the show. I can end the gallery relationship. I can put out one paragraph about your "health" and you will never be taken seriously in this city again. I will ruin you and it will take me a week.
s02.chats.wa_015: Studio. Nine. We're settling this tonight.
s02.chats.wa_016: I've calmed down. Whatever you think happened tonight, it didn't. Call me.

s02.mail.gm_011.body:
Hanna,

Read it twice. I'm not going to fall apart about it — I've known the shape of this for a year, I just didn't have the numbers.

Don't send anything else to my email. Put it in the drive.

s02.mail.gm_020.subject: (no subject)
s02.mail.gm_020.body:
Juno,

If you're reading this then I've sent it, which means something went wrong, which means I'm sorry.

I've spent two years being managed. Not represented — managed. He has the passwords to accounts with my name on them. He decides which rooms I'm allowed to be in. When I found the money I thought: good, now it's simple, now I can just show someone. And then I understood that showing someone means a solicitor, and eighteen months, and him in the same city the whole time telling everyone I'm unwell.

There is a version of this where I get to be free next week instead of in two years. I keep looking at it.

You'd hate it. That's how I know it's bad.

I'm not sending this.

M

s02.notes.note_002.title: What Hanna found
s02.notes.note_002.block_001: A company called Halcyon, which is a bird that supposedly calms the sea, which is the most Leo thing I have ever heard.
s02.notes.note_002.block_002: Two years of it. Six of the transfers happened AFTER I asked to see the books. He didn't stop. He didn't even slow down. He simply assumed I wouldn't be able to do anything.
s02.notes.note_002.block_003: The horrible part is that he might be right.
s02.notes.note_003.block_001: If I go to a solicitor: eighteen months minimum, he stays in the city, he talks to everyone, and the show doesn't happen. I looked all of this up. It is not pessimism, it is arithmetic.
s02.notes.note_003.block_002: If I go to the police with the money: they take a statement about a civil dispute. He is a man with a lawyer. I am an artist who posts about insomnia.
s02.notes.note_003.block_003: If Maya Sorensen stops existing on the 7th, everything he did becomes evidence in a much bigger file, and someone else has to carry it. Not me. Someone with a licence.
s02.notes.note_003.block_004: Everything about the money stays true. I don't have to invent a single number. I only have to invent one night.
s02.notes.note_003.block_005: Old accounts to bring back up: forum login, the drive, the laptop. Handle is still moth. Machine is still atelier. Nobody has looked at either since I was fifteen and nobody will look now.

s02.memos.vm_001.title: Studio 4
s02.memos.vm_001.transcript:
[recording begins mid-sentence]

BRANDT: — sign it and then we talk about the accounting like adults.

SORENSEN: I'm not signing six years of everything I make.

BRANDT: You signed the first one.

SORENSEN: I was twenty-four and you were my boyfriend.

BRANDT: [pause] Don't do that.

SORENSEN: Say the number, Leo. Say it out loud and I'll sign it tonight.

BRANDT: There is no number. There's a business you don't understand and a woman who has decided she's a victim because an accountant flattered her.

SORENSEN: One hundred and eighty thousand.

BRANDT: [long pause] I'm going to go, and you're going to think about what you're doing to yourself here.

[door]
s02.memos.vm_002.title: after Hanna
s02.memos.vm_002.transcript: One hundred and eighty. I said it out loud in the kitchen and it didn't sound like a real amount of money, it sounded like a phone number. Two years. Every time I said I was tired he said the fees were the price of being taken seriously, and I believed him, because I wanted to be taken seriously more than I wanted to be able to count.
s02.memos.vm_003.title: 3am
s02.memos.vm_003.transcript: There's a version where I do this properly. Solicitors, statements, eighteen months of being the difficult woman. And there's a version where it takes a week. I know which one is right. I also know which one I'm going to pick, and I'd like to say that on a recording so that at least one honest account of it exists somewhere.
s02.memos.vm_004.title: wall text
s02.memos.vm_004.transcript: For the wall text: the work is about things that keep their shape after the thing inside them is gone. Don't write "vessel" in the wall text, it's already the title, they'll think I'm simple.

s02.ending.expose: The transfers hold up and Leo Brandt goes down for the theft. The murder charge collapses the moment prosecutors are handed a victim who is still breathing, and the forged door log becomes an obstruction file with Maya Sorensen's name at the top of it. She is charged in absentia. She stops running only in the sense that there is nowhere left to run to.
s02.ending.fraud_only: You file the money and keep the rest. Brandt draws four years for fraud and walks out able to say, truthfully, that he was never charged with hurting anyone. The Berlin file stays open with Maya Sorensen listed as its victim — which is the only reason she is still free. She does not thank you. She never writes again.
s02.ending.silence: The phone stays closed. Brandt keeps the money and the story, the file gathers dust, and a woman declared dead in March stays dead on paper, which is what she asked for in the first place. Juno leaves flowers on an empty grave every spring. You are the only person alive who knows they are unnecessary.

s02.memos.vm_010.title: Room tone — Studio 4
s02.memos.vm_010.transcript: [thirty seconds of an empty room: the extractor, a lorry outside, something ticking as it cools] That's the ceiling. That's what I keep hearing at night and thinking it's someone on the stairs. Right. Fine. It's the ceiling.
s02.memos.vm_011.transcript: I'm going to say it out loud so it stops going round. The piece is not about surveillance. Everyone will say it's about surveillance because there are twelve screens and a corridor. It's about the eleven seconds. It's about the fact that you can watch a thing happen twelve times and still not be there when it happens. If I can't say that in one sentence to Kasimir on the twenty-first then I've made something I can't explain, which is the same as not having made it.

s02.notes.note_011.title: Things that only work at 4am
s02.notes.note_011.block_001: A room you cannot photograph. Every attempt comes out as a different room. Not a trick of the lens — a trick of the light doing something the sensor will not agree to.
s02.notes.note_011.block_002: Twelve screens, all showing the same corridor, all eleven seconds apart. You would have to stand there for two minutes before you understood what you were looking at, and most people give a piece nine seconds.
s02.notes.note_011.block_003: Sound only. A room with nothing in it and a recording of that same room with someone in it. Juno would know how to do this and would tell me it has been done.
s02.notes.note_011.block_004: Something honest for once. Discarded on the grounds that I do not know what that would look like.
